title: AI Platform Agents: what it uses
lede: One arrow for each component this feature lists. The steps reuse the feature's own "how it works" text; nothing here is a new claim. Internal and confidential: this text comes from an internal Ping deck and has not been tested on our tenant.

steps.title: Thirteen agent sources
steps.what: AI Platform Agents gives inventory, permission review and remediation for AI agents across thirteen sources: AWS Bedrock Agents, AWS Bedrock AgentCore, Amazon Lex, Amazon Bedrock Flows, Google Vertex AI Agent Engine, Google Agent Builder, Google Agent Registry, Dialogflow CX, Azure AI Foundry, Microsoft Copilot Studio, Salesforce Agentforce, Databricks Mosaic AI and Snowflake Cortex AI.
steps.why: Agents created in cloud consoles sit outside identity processes: nobody inventoried them and nobody knows what they reach.

steps.title: Cross-cloud inventory
steps.what: The cross-cloud inventory lists every agent with its identity, model, configuration and owner, including A2A-native agents from the GCP Agent Registry with their agent cards.
steps.why: Agents created in cloud consoles sit outside identity processes: nobody inventoried them and nobody knows what they reach.

steps.title: AWS Organizations onboarding
steps.what: AWS Organizations member accounts are enumerated and onboarded automatically, scoped by organizational unit.
steps.why: Agents created in cloud consoles sit outside identity processes: nobody inventoried them and nobody knows what they reach.

steps.title: Risk scoring, five levels and 46 findings
steps.what: Risk scoring gives a five-level score built from 46 specific findings, among them administrative privilege, publicly reachable and unauthenticated agents, over-privileged identity, lateral-movement and credential-exfiltration paths, dangling roles, missing guardrails and deprecated models, and more.
steps.why: Agents created in cloud consoles sit outside identity processes: nobody inventoried them and nobody knows what they reach.

steps.title: Custodian ownership
steps.what: Every agent can be assigned a custodian, so an orphaned agent has a named owner.
steps.why: Agents created in cloud consoles sit outside identity processes: nobody inventoried them and nobody knows what they reach.

steps.title: Delete and quarantine remediation
steps.what: Remediation offers delete on twelve of thirteen sources (Databricks in development) and quarantine on nine (the slide names Bedrock Agents, AgentCore, Lex, Vertex AI, Copilot Studio, Agentforce and Snowflake Cortex), plus targeted fixes: strip over-privileged roles, stop a privileged flow, disable a named credential, retag or reconfigure.
steps.why: Agents created in cloud consoles sit outside identity processes: nobody inventoried them and nobody knows what they reach.
